text:
Maria: Heads-up — nightly-e2e turned red when the job was scheduled across two nodes (shard A on node gpus-uk1-03, shard B on gpus-uk1-07). It looks like a mixed driver/ABI situation + OOM on the second shard.

Maria: Error snippet from the failing task:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "run_inference.py", line 312, in <module>
    out = model.generate(inp)
RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid device function
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 1; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 36.50 GiB already allocated)
```

Maria: Quick note — node gpus-uk1-03 reports nvidia-smi driver 535.104, gpus-uk1-07 has 535.089 (we rolled a partial driver bump this morning).

David: ugh, that mismatch would explain the `invalid device function` on older driver. Does the CI scheduler prefer packing shards across nodes? This test is supposed to be single-node but the new shard-split change bumped parallelism.

Ash: Can you repro by pinning the job to one host? If single-node passes, it's almost certainly a driver skew. Also try setting `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` to force single GPU in the container to see if the OOM is just cross-device accounting.

Maria: repro attempt: pinned to gpus-uk1-03 (newer driver) — passes. Pinned to gpus-uk1-07 (older driver) — fails with same `invalid device function`. So reproducible on-host.

Priya: OK that narrows it. Two actions: 1) mark the nightly job to require homogeneous drivers (temp fix), 2) ask infra to roll gpus-uk1-07 to 535.104. I'll open infra ticket.

Maria: For triage, I'll attach a minimal repro command you can run locally on the node:
```bash
# ssh to node and run inside CI image
docker run --gpus all -it --entrypoint /bin/bash registry.redwood-ci/nightly:latest -c '
  export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 && python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.driver_version, torch.cuda.is_available())"'
```

Ash: Also collect `dmesg | tail -n 200` and `nvidia-smi -q > /tmp/nv-qa.txt` from the failing host. If we see PTX/JIT warnings or XIDs, attach them.

infra-bot: New ticket created: INFRA-4321 — "driver drift gpus-uk1-07 -> target 535.104". Assigned to infra-team oncall. ETA: canary reimage in 2h.

oncall-bot: Re-run requested — requeued nightly-e2e shard for gpus-uk1-07-only (job 87432). Please monitor.

David: If infra can't roll quickly, we should gate the change that allows cross-node placement for this test. Priya, can you add a temporary label/constraint in the pipeline config?

Priya: On it — adding `nodeAffinity: homogeneous-drivers=true` to the job spec and kicking a single-nightly run.

Maria: Thanks. I'll keep the thread updated with `dmesg` + `nv-qa.txt` once infra finishes the canary. Also dropping a note to the release notes that partial driver rollouts can break older kernels.

Ash: Follow-up: consider adding a small CI smoke that detects driver versions on candidate nodes before spreading shards. Cheap check: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader` and fail early with a clear message.

Maria: Agreed — low-effort guard. Marking this thread: action items -> INFRA-4321 (roll), PR-xxxx (pipeline affinity), add smoke check.

David: tl;dr: failure = driver skew across nodes causing invalid device function + then OOM symptoms when fallback/codegen differs. Fix = roll drivers or force single-node until fleet is homogeneous.

Maria: Will update when infra confirms canary success. :thumbsup:
